product_info.name: Wells Fargo Active Cash Credit Card

terms_analysis.key_information:
Key Points:
• APR ranges from 19.24% to 29.24% for purchases (varies with Prime Rate), which is typical for mainstream credit cards
• No annual fee and 2% cash back on all purchases - this combination is better than most cards in the market
• Pro: 25+ day grace period means no interest if you pay in full each month - standard but crucial benefit
• Con: Balance transfer fee up to 5% is on the high end compared to cards offering 3% or promotional 0% fees
terms_analysis.risks:
Potential Risks:
• [MEDIUM] Mandatory arbitration clause prevents class-action lawsuits and jury trials - very common in credit cards.
  Impact: Must resolve disputes through arbitration instead of court, potentially limiting your legal options
terms_analysis.consumer_score:
Credit Card Consumer Score: 58/100 (Mediocre)
Interpretation: This is an average mainstream credit card - the no annual fee and cash back rewards are positives, but the moderate-to-high APR range makes it costly if you carry a balance. Best for those who pay in full monthly.
terms_analysis.details:
Details:
• Interest rates: 19.24%-29.24% APR for purchases/balance transfers; 29.99% for cash advances
• Fees: No annual fee; $40 late payment fee; 5% balance transfer fee; 5% or $10 cash advance fee
• Rewards: 2% unlimited cash back on all purchases with no caps or categories
• Payment terms: Minimum payment is 1% of balance plus interest and fees, or $25 (whichever is greater)
• Dispute resolution: Binding arbitration required; cannot join class-action lawsuits

reddit_insights.positive:
• 2% cash back on all purchases with no annual fee
• $200 welcome bonus and cell phone insurance included
• Easy redemption and potential future travel point transfers
reddit_insights.negative:
• 3% foreign transaction fee makes it less ideal for travel
• Credit limit increases can be difficult to obtain
• Tied to Wells Fargo, which some users view skeptically
